The Trial Chamber has understandably restricted our cross-examination to the issue admissibility. We will not be in a position to know whether we need then to cross-examine Mr. Graham in the event, one, the interview is ruled admissible until the question of admissibility as against the other accused is also decided upon, because of course the questions we might ask so far as that's concerned are completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're hundred per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And -- yes. Well, I don't need say any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Judge Prost will be answering your question, Mr. McCloskey, and more or less it draws from a point that we made when we first started discussing this when we called on Mr. Lazarevic to be more precise in -- in his submissions and at least give us an indication of what he was contesting within the framework of admissibility. So Judge Prost, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Yes. Basically it's as the President has indicated, Mr. McCloskey. We anticipate the issue of admissibility to be a confined one in this instance based on the grounds of which counsel for Mr. Borovcanin had already outlined to you as the basis for the legal arguments which will be advanced in relation to the admissibility issue. It is certainly broader than just voluntariness because he made reference to things such as adequate representation, the nature of the cautions that were given, things of that nature. So it is not strictly just in a pure common law tradition of voluntariness, but it is not in our view a question that goes to the broader issues of overall credibility, how questions were put in the sense of assessing the substance of the interview. We expect the arguments, the cross-examinations, and the submissions to focus on admissibility issues of that nature include voluntariness. Obviously, some of the other counsel may identify some other legal issues and those may have been determined case by case as they relate to admissibility, but we are not anticipating a broad ranging challenge that deals with the substance of the interview. It is restricted as indicated to what's been identified as the legal issues to admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but he's reframed it in a rather different way today. We are also answering your posit, namely, that according to you it's more appropriate that this audio recording be played before we start this whole process. Our answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- based on the -- the clarification, I would agree. With those limited issues, there is -- it's not appropriate to play -- play it, but I was going on the way I -- we viewed admissibility in the intercept context, which was everything, but -- and so I thank you for that clarification. And -- however, as I would request that it has -- other Defences have legal issues along the same lines that we be allowed to hear them now as would be appropriate for any legal issues, especially regarding admissibility. It is normal to receive this information in writing, which is fine. We don't need that. But we should have some idea of where they're planning -- where others are planning to go. If it's within the context of Mr. Lazarevic's statements, fine, but if there's something new -- legal issues are not the kind of thing that pop up in the middle of a discussion -- I mean, in the middle of a hearing like this. These are issues that people are prepared for and that the Prosecution should have notice of. If there's anything new. If there's not, we're fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Does any one of the Defence team wish to address this issue? Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I would ask till close of business tomorrow for the remaining six accused to notify the Prosecution in writing as to whether any further issues arise. It's simply not a question I could answer at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that's fair enough. That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Agreed. So you will have until the end of business of tomorrow -- tomorrow's Friday. Okay. Yes. Does anyone wish to address the Chamber on anything else? Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. With your permission, I'd like to address the Chamber with regard to a delicate subject, and I would like to do it in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now, and if there is no other business to transact, we will adjourn. Please be prepared with Alistair Graham on Tuesday and with -- as I explained, the possibility -- either two possibilities. We can't tell you whether we will require the use of that tape. Thank you. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.44 a.m.,
